The Regional Program Manager (RPM) owns delivery of the ERTS Commercial Compliance Program within an assigned multi-state region. The RPM is the primary technical and commercial point of contact for program clients in the region.

The program spans OSHA, EPA, and DOT HMT requirements, plus the state programs that apply in the region. The ideal candidate has a consulting or multi-site practitioner background, is comfortable in a client facing environment, and can translate regulatory findings into practical corrective actions and sellable follow up work.

Clean Harbors is the leading provider of environmental, energy and industrial services throughout the United States, Canada, Mexico and Puerto Rico. Everywhere industry meets environment, Clean Harbors is on-site, providing premier environmental, energy and industrial services. We are solving tough problems through innovation and proven methodology – come be part of the solution with us.

This position is located and supports the Western Region of the US.

Why work for Clean Harbors?

Health and Safety is our #1 priority and we live it 3-6-5!
Focus on maintaining sustainability and cleaning the Earth
Recruiting Pay range of $110,000-$120,000
Comprehensive health benefits coverage after 30 days of full-time employment including 401K with Company match
Own part of the company with our Employee Stock Purchase Plan
Opportunities for growth and development for all the stages of your career
Company paid training and tuition reimbursement

Responsibilities

Program and Client Management

Manage all Commercial Compliance Program accounts in the region: onboarding, annual service calendars, scheduling of site visits, and delivery of services.
Serve as the single point of contact for regional clients; conduct kickoff and close meetings, present findings to leadership, and manage escalations.
Track utilization, billable hours, and deliverable status; maintain accurate client records, inspection reports, training rosters, and corrective action logs.
Coordinate and quality-check subcontractors for specialty scopes.
Identify upsell and cross-sell opportunities and hand off or close in coordination with sales.

Compliance Services

Perform on-site compliance audits and gap analyses against regulatory requirements and best practices.
Conduct hazard assessments including PPE hazard assessments, job hazard analyses, and facility walkthroughs; document findings with regulatory citations, risk ranking, and recommended corrective actions.
Review client hazardous waste program and storage areas: generator category determinations and episodic generation, waste determinations, accumulation area inspections, contingency plan reviews, biennial reports, manifest recordkeeping
Deliver monthly inspection program tools and safety communications ('safety splashes') to program clients.
Support clients during agency inspections and in responding to OSHA citations, EPA or state notices of violation, and consent orders.

Training Delivery

Develop and deliver on-site and virtual EH&S training, including OSHA HAZWOPER and general industry topics, RCRA Hazardous Waste, DOT Hazardous Materials.
Assist clients with maintain training records to satisfy regulatory documentation requirements and support client audit defense.

Regional Regulatory Awareness

Maintain working knowledge of state-plan OSHA programs and state-authorized RCRA programs in the assigned region and advise clients where state requirements are more stringent than federal.
Monitor regulatory changes affecting program clients and brief the Director and client contacts.

Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree in occupational safety and health, Environmental Science, Industrial Hygiene, Engineering, Chemistry, or a closely related technical field.

Experience

Seven to ten years of progressive EHS experience, including at least three years performing compliance audits or inspections across multiple sites or multiple clients.
Demonstrated hands-on experience with both general industry safety programs (29 CFR 1910) and RCRA hazardous waste generator compliance (40 CFR Parts 260 to 262).
Experience delivering EHS training to hourly and supervisory audiences.
Experience in an environmental or EHS consulting firm, or in a multi-site corporate EHS role with external client or vendor-facing responsibility.

40-Hour HAZWOPER

DOT hazmat employee training
Proficiency with Microsoft Office and web-based EHS data platforms; ability to write clear, citation-supported technical reports.

Board certification. One or more board certifications: Certified Safety Professional (CSP) or Associate Safety Professional (ASP) from BCSP; Certified Hazardous Materials Manager (CHMM) from IHMM; Certified Industrial Hygienist (CIH) from BGC; or OHST/CHST from BCSP.
Management systems. ISO 14001 / ISO 45001 lead auditor or internal auditor training; experience with EHS management system audits.
Adjacent programs. Experience with SPCC plans, Tier II reporting, & stormwater (NPDES MSGP).
Advanced degree. Master's degree in related discipline.

The Information Management Program Manager provides senior leadership for Kiewit’s Industrial District Project Information Management (PIM) Program and Information Management/Document Control organization. This role is responsible for building and leading a high-performing information management function that supports project execution, strengthens governance, develops talent, and drives consistent information practices across the industrial market.

This position partners with engineering and operations leadership, functional leaders, and project teams to standardize execution, improve processes, align systems and workflows, and ensure project information is controlled from startup through final turnover and closeout.

District Overview

Kiewit’s Industrial District delivers complex construction and engineering projects across North America, including advanced technology, power, industrial, and other large-scale markets. Our teams operate in fast-paced project environments that require disciplined execution, strong coordination, and reliable information management. This role is key to helping project teams establish the standards, systems, and controls needed to manage project information effectively throughout the full project lifecycle.

Serve as the district leader and primary champion for the Project Information Management Program.
Lead development, deployment, and continuous improvement of district PIM standards, procedures, playbooks, tools, and assurance processes.
Influence operations, functional leaders, and project teams to align information management requirements with project needs and delivery models.
Establish district-wide governance, metrics, reporting requirements, and assurance processes.
Drive consistency across engineering, procurement, construction, startup, commissioning, turnover, and final records management.
Lead staffing projections, recruiting support, resource planning, and project deployment strategy for Information Management/Document Control personnel.
Develop talent through onboarding, mentoring, career development, succession planning, and leadership coaching.

Assist projects in developing information management strategies based on project size, complexity, client requirements, and delivery model.
Support implementation of Engineering Information Management, Trade Partner Information Management (TPIM), Vendor Data Management, and Turnover Information Management programs.

Strengthen information handoffs from Construction and Quality through completions, commissioning, turnover, client deliverables, and archive.

Lead district deployment of Trade Partner Information Management (TPIM) standards and practices.
Establish governance for trade partner submittals, vendor data, design-assist deliverables, delegated design information, quality documentation, and turnover requirements.
Translate client and contract documentation requirements into RFQ, subcontract, vendor, quality, turnover, and final records expectations.
Support pre-award evaluation and onboarding of Trade Partners around systems, submittals, RFIs, quality documentation, delegated design, and turnover requirements.

Systems, Technology & Reporting

Partner with business technology, systems administrators, and project teams to establish systems-of-record and platform governance.
Drive standardization of metadata, numbering, workflows, templates, reporting, and dashboards.
Lead implementation, governance, and optimization of InEight, TeamBinder, SharePoint, Procore, CxAlloy, Power BI, and other approved information platforms.
Develop district metrics and executive dashboards for information readiness, compliance, submittal performance, vendor data, change management, turnover readiness, and final records completion.

Build team capability through onboarding, training, mentoring, career development, and succession planning.
Evaluate emerging industry trends and delivery models and recommend improvements to district standards.

Bachelor’s degree in Engineering, Construction Management, Project Controls, Information Management, Business, or a related field.

Project Controls

Information Management
Engineering Management
Construction Management
Quality Management

Experience with InEight, TeamBinder, SharePoint, Procore, Power BI, completions/commissioning platforms such as CxAlloy, or similar information management systems.

Experience supporting EPC, Design-Build, Advanced Technology, or complex mega-projects.

About The Role

The Manufacturing Data Analyst plays a critical role in transforming raw manufacturing data into actionable insights that drive operational efficiency and product quality improvements. This position involves analyzing complex datasets from production lines, identifying trends, and providing data-driven recommendations to optimize manufacturing processes. The analyst collaborates closely with engineering, quality assurance, and production teams to support continuous improvement initiatives and reduce waste. By leveraging advanced analytical techniques and tools, the role ensures that manufacturing decisions are supported by accurate and timely data. Ultimately, the Manufacturing Data Analyst contributes to enhancing overall manufacturing performance and competitiveness in the market.

Minimum Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree in Data Science, Statistics, Industrial Engineering, Manufacturing Engineering, or a related field.
Proficiency in data analysis tools such as SQL, Excel, and statistical software (e.g., R, Python).
Experience working with manufacturing data or in a manufacturing environment.
Strong analytical and problem-solving skills with attention to detail.
Excellent communication skills to effectively convey complex data insights to non-technical stakeholders.

Preferred Qualifications

Master’s degree in a relevant field or equivalent work experience.
Familiarity with manufacturing execution systems (MES) and enterprise resource planning (ERP) software.
Experience with data visualization tools such as Tableau, Power BI, or similar platforms.
Knowledge of Six Sigma, Lean Manufacturing, or other continuous improvement methodologies.
Programming experience in Python or R for advanced data analysis and automation.

Responsibilities

Collect, clean, and analyze manufacturing data from various sources including production equipment, sensors, and enterprise systems.
Develop and maintain dashboards and reports to monitor key performance indicators (KPIs) related to production efficiency, quality, and downtime.
Identify patterns, anomalies, and root causes of manufacturing issues through statistical analysis and data mining techniques.
Collaborate with cross-functional teams to design experiments and pilot projects aimed at process optimization and defect reduction.
Present findings and actionable insights to stakeholders through clear visualizations and detailed reports to support decision-making.

Skills

The Manufacturing Data Analyst uses required skills such as SQL and Excel daily to extract and manipulate large datasets from manufacturing systems, ensuring data accuracy and completeness. Statistical software like R or Python is employed to perform in-depth analyses, identify trends, and build predictive models that inform process improvements. Communication skills are essential for translating complex analytical results into clear, actionable insights that can be understood by production and management teams. Preferred skills like familiarity with MES and ERP systems enhance the analyst’s ability to integrate data from multiple sources, providing a comprehensive view of manufacturing operations. Additionally, expertise in data visualization tools allows the analyst to create intuitive dashboards that facilitate real-time monitoring and decision-making.

Overview Statement Rn Care Coordinator (case Manager)

BWH CARE CONTINUUM

The RN Care Coordinator (RNCC) manages a caseload of patients and is responsible for ensuring care that supports desired clinical and financial outcomes. Coordinating the care prescribed by an interdisciplinary team, the RNCC utilizes patient assessment, care guidelines, protocols, payer regulations and response to therapies to assess the episode of illness from pre admission to post discharge. Mobilizes resources to maximize efficiency of care delivery.

Care Facilitation Coordinates and insures implementation of the plan of care, utilizing case management principles.
Prior to or within 24-48 hours of admission the RNCC, by interview of the patient/family, discussion with physician team and/or attending MD and other team members, develops a provisional treatment program and tentative discharge date.
Reviews daily treatment plan with physicians, nurses and patient / families to insure interdisciplinary communication and coordination is occurring.
Participates with nursing staff and physicians in patient care rounds to contribute to plan of care and monitor and report patient progress.

Initiates contact with home health agencies and extended care facilities to insure prompt and effective transition of care.

Collaborates with appropriate individuals, departments, and payers to insure appropriateness of admission, continued days of stay, and reimbursement.

Identifies SNF and AND days for Medicare and Medicaid patients.

For more than 50 years, Ocean Conservancy has delivered effective, evidence-based solutions for the ocean and all who depend on it. Today, we continue to unite science, people and policy to protect our ocean from the greatest challenges it faces: climate change, plastic pollution and biodiversity loss. We are a 501(C)3 headquartered in Washington, D.C. that inspires a worldwide network of partners, advocates and supporters through our comprehensive and clear-eyed approach to ocean conservation. Together, we are securing a healthy ocean and a thriving planet, forever and for everyone.

Position Summary

As a core member of Ocean Conservancy’s Florida Conservation Team, the Florida Conservation Program Manager

The Manager will serve as a key point of contact with both existing and new local government partners, and will provide lead flagship projects such as grassroots marine debris efforts, marine plastics assessments and grassroots advocacy, sea level rise and climate change initiatives, water quality and abundance interventions, and marine wildlife and habitat protection efforts. The Manager will also represent Ocean Conservancy in public appearances, testimony, and in outreach and education activities.

The Manager will report to the Senior Director of Florida Conservation, and will preferably be based in St. Petersburg, Florida.

About The Role

The Manufacturing Data Analyst plays a critical role in transforming raw manufacturing data into actionable insights that drive operational efficiency and product quality improvements. This position involves analyzing complex datasets from production lines, identifying trends, and providing data-driven recommendations to optimize manufacturing processes. The analyst collaborates closely with engineering, quality assurance, and production teams to support continuous improvement initiatives and reduce waste. By leveraging advanced analytical techniques and tools, the role ensures that manufacturing decisions are supported by accurate and timely data. Ultimately, the Manufacturing Data Analyst contributes to enhancing overall manufacturing performance and competitiveness in the market.

Minimum Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree in Data Science, Statistics, Industrial Engineering, Manufacturing Engineering, or a related field.
Proficiency in data analysis tools such as SQL, Excel, and statistical software (e.g., R, Python).
Experience working with manufacturing data or in a manufacturing environment.
Strong analytical and problem-solving skills with attention to detail.
Excellent communication skills to effectively convey complex data insights to non-technical stakeholders.

Preferred Qualifications

Master’s degree in a relevant field or equivalent work experience.
Familiarity with manufacturing execution systems (MES) and enterprise resource planning (ERP) software.
Experience with data visualization tools such as Tableau, Power BI, or similar platforms.
Knowledge of Six Sigma, Lean Manufacturing, or other continuous improvement methodologies.
Programming experience in Python or R for advanced data analysis and automation.

Responsibilities

Collect, clean, and analyze manufacturing data from various sources including production equipment, sensors, and enterprise systems.
Develop and maintain dashboards and reports to monitor key performance indicators (KPIs) related to production efficiency, quality, and downtime.
Identify patterns, anomalies, and root causes of manufacturing issues through statistical analysis and data mining techniques.
Collaborate with cross-functional teams to design experiments and pilot projects aimed at process optimization and defect reduction.
Present findings and actionable insights to stakeholders through clear visualizations and detailed reports to support decision-making.

Skills

The Manufacturing Data Analyst uses required skills such as SQL and Excel daily to extract and manipulate large datasets from manufacturing systems, ensuring data accuracy and completeness. Statistical software like R or Python is employed to perform in-depth analyses, identify trends, and build predictive models that inform process improvements. Communication skills are essential for translating complex analytical results into clear, actionable insights that can be understood by production and management teams. Preferred skills like familiarity with MES and ERP systems enhance the analyst’s ability to integrate data from multiple sources, providing a comprehensive view of manufacturing operations. Additionally, expertise in data visualization tools allows the analyst to create intuitive dashboards that facilitate real-time monitoring and decision-making.
